question: do per-lineage delta-magnitude ratios (vs K562, on shared essential-screen targets) motivate per-context delta_scale?

method.delta_definition: pseudobulk_mean(perturbed) - pseudobulk_mean(non-targeting controls), L2 norm per target

sources.Jurkat: HF bendidiihab/tx_evaluation nadig_2024_jurkat.h5ad (262,956 cells; per-target means via chunked one-hot groupby; 2 corrupt HDF5 blocks skipped ~1.5% cells)
sources.hESC: no essential screen; ratio from k012 paired-transfer LOO scalar fit (47 pairs)

hESC.note: LOO-fitted global scalar, K562->hESC, 47 paired targets

figshare_gwps_inventory: only K562 has a genome-wide arm; rpe1_*/jurkat/hepg2 public files are the 2393-gene essential screen
scale_map_logic: scale_ctx = 1.7 (champion) x ratio_ctx / mean(ratios); mean(ratios)~1.0 -> A=1.7x1.01, B=1.7x1.57, C=1.7x0.44
interpretation: Uniform x1.7 was likely a mixture optimum: B genuinely wants ~1.6x (RPE1 deltas are 1.57x K562's), A wants ~1.0x, C likely less

Directional similarity also varies: cos(K562,Jurkat)=0.47 > cos(K562,RPE1)=0.30 >> cos(K562,hESC)~0.13 — Jurkat is the most transferable lineage despite context A's strong Jurkat identity being most 'foreign' to K562
Essential screens cover 0/300 panel targets — they can only supply transfer supervision / magnitude ratios, never direct deltas
caveats: ratios measured on essential genes; panel is non-essential — magnitude relationship may differ
norm ratios conflate biology with per-dataset normalization
B (0.369) and C (0.379) lineage assignments are weak
Atlas-sourced deltas (4 targets) are already context-appropriate but get scaled in the assembled delta
